title: US 10-Year Treasury Yield Rises Ahead of Powe... | Forex News...
content: The 10‑year U.S. Treasury yield rose to 4.33% on Friday as investors awaited Federal Reserve Chair Jerome Powell’s address at Jackson Hole. Market analysts assign a 65% probability to a rate cut in September and anticipate roughly 50 basis points of easing in 2025. Despite hawkish remarks from other Fed officials and a decline in interest‑rate swaps, uncertainty remains about the timing and size of any cuts. Powell is expected to stress that a September decision will depend on forthcoming employment and inflation data, thereby preserving policy flexibility. Investors anticipate that Powell will note signs of economic weakness but will not commit to immediate rate reductions.

title: 10-Year Yield Rebounds on Hot Data | Forex News 2025.08.21 (en)
content: The 10‑year U.S. Treasury yield rose to 4.33% on Thursday, a move that strengthens hawkish sentiment within the Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC).  The S&P Purchasing Managers' Index (PMI) reached its highest level this year, signalling robust growth in new business activity.  The PMI survey also reported that companies are raising selling prices at the steepest rate in three years, a trend that aligns with the Philadelphia Federal Reserve’s inflation gauge hitting a three‑year peak.  Minutes from the most recent FOMC meeting revealed that policymakers largely believe "inflationary threats outweigh concerns about a weaker labor market" and warned that inflation expectations could become unanchored.  Despite these concerns, the labor market remains mixed: the S&P report noted positive labor trends, but the Department of Labor’s continuing jobless claims have risen to the highest level since 2021.  Federal Reserve Chair Jerome Powell is scheduled to speak tomorrow, which may shed light on future rate policy.

title: 30-Jähriger US-Treasury: Zinsanstieg setzt sich fort
content: The 30‑year U.S. Treasury yield rose sharply to 4.76% today, a 3‑basis‑point gain over yesterday’s close and a 0.63% increase during the session, extending a two‑day upward trend that added 0.075 percentage points overall. The move is largely driven by macro‑economic factors: the Federal Reserve cut rates by 25 basis points earlier this week, and Fed Chair Powell warned that there are "keine risikofreien Wege" (no risk‑free paths), adding uncertainty. Recent economic data support the sentiment: initial jobless‑claims were lower than expected, the Congressional Budget Office forecast a temporary slowdown, inflation is projected to stay above target for the next two years, and the New York Fed’s DSGE model expects stronger growth and lower inflation in 2025. Technically, the yield is testing a recent resistance level at 4.75%, its highest since September 5, and markets are watching whether that level can hold. The broader bond market mirrors the trend, with the 10‑year Treasury up 2 basis points to 4.13% and the 2‑year Treasury up 1 basis point to 3.58%. Equity markets are mixed but slightly positive, with the S&P 500 and Nasdaq Composite showing modest gains, while the U.S. dollar index rose 0.17% on Fed‑policy support. Commodity prices varied: WTI crude fell 0.30% to $63.38 per barrel, and gold rose 0.6% to $3,665.54 per ounce. The VIX volatility index remained below 15, indicating relatively low market fear despite underlying uncertainties. A recent Treasury Yield 30‑Years Index analysis released on September 19 urges investors to take urgent action, questioning whether to buy or sell.

title: Kursgewinne
content: US Treasury prices rose on Wednesday, with the ten‑year Treasury note future up 0.14% to 113.50 points and the yield on ten‑year U.S. bonds falling to 4.05%. The gains were driven by expectations of a rate cut, supported by a sharp decline in producer prices. In August, producer prices rose 2.6% year‑on‑year, below economists’ forecast of 3.3%. Producer prices tend to influence consumer prices, which the Fed uses to guide monetary policy. August inflation data will be released Thursday.

title: US 10-Year Yield Rebounds Further | Forex News 2025.09.18 (en)
content: The yield on the 10‑year U.S. Treasury note rose to 4.1% on Thursday, rebounding from a five‑month low of under 4% that followed the Federal Reserve’s rate decision. The Fed cut its key policy rate by 25 basis points and signaled the possibility of two additional cuts later this year, while noting that core inflation may exceed earlier estimates and that economic growth and employment forecasts have improved. Chairman Powell’s remarks suggested that the single rate cut does not necessarily signal a trend toward further monetary easing. A decline in unemployment claims and strong readings in the Philadelphia Fed’s activity index have alleviated concerns about a weakening labor market, adding upward pressure on Treasury yields. Meanwhile, the Fed has kept its quantitative tightening stance, even as the drawdown in overnight reverse repurchase agreements has been significant. These developments collectively support the recent uptick in the 10‑year yield.

title: 两年2万亿！美联储能"鲸吞"下所有美国政府新发短债？
content: According to a report by Morgan Stanley, the Federal Reserve may purchase nearly $20 trillion in short-term Treasury securities over the next two years, which could cover the entire short-term Treasury issuance of the US Treasury Department during the same period. This would be a significant help to the US Treasury Department, which has been relying heavily on short-term debt to finance its operations. Morgan Stanley analysts Mark Cabana and Katie Craig believe that the Fed's potential shift in its Treasury holdings could provide a much-needed funding boost to the Treasury Department. Cabana estimates that if the Fed were to reinvest the proceeds from maturing mortgage-backed securities (MBS) in short-term Treasury securities and gradually replace maturing long-term Treasuries with short-term debt, the scale of this operation could be around $1 trillion per year. The report also suggests that the Fed could increase its short-term Treasury holdings by 50% of its assets, mainly to match its short-term liabilities, including reserve balances and reverse repurchase agreements, and to absorb changes in the Treasury General Account (TGA) cash balances. Morgan Stanley estimates that if the Treasury Department maintains its long-term Treasury auction size stable until October 2026, the short-term Treasury supply in 2026 would be $825 billion, and in 2027, it would be $1.067 trillion. The report concludes that if the Fed were to take this step, it would help ensure a strong demand for short-term government debt, thereby alleviating concerns about the potential liquidity crunch caused by the Treasury Department's large-scale debt issuance.

title: Treasury Yields Rise | Forex News 2025.10.06 (en)
content: The yield on the US 10-year Treasury note rose to 4.16% on October 6, 2025, marking its highest level in over a week. This increase was partly driven by rising borrowing costs in Europe and Japan due to recent political developments. Market attention is also focused on the ongoing US federal government shutdown, now in its sixth day, which has delayed the release of key economic data and prompted President Trump to warn of potential federal employee dismissals. While last week's private-sector data showed a weak labor market and slowing demand, these indicators did not immediately raise concerns about broader economic growth. Investors are now awaiting new commentary from central bank officials and the release of the Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) minutes for further signals on future monetary policy.

title: Treasury Yield 30 Years Index: Ein Step-by-Step-Fortschritt
content: The yield on 30-year U.S. Treasury bonds rose sharply to 4.762% on October 6, 2025, an increase of 5.2 basis points from Friday’s close. Despite the ongoing U.S. government shutdown since October 1, 2024, long-term yields have shown surprising resilience. Typically considered safe-haven assets, Treasuries are seeing upward pressure due to market concerns over the shutdown. Investors are also awaiting the Federal Reserve’s meeting minutes later in the week for clues on the pace of potential interest rate cuts. Technically, the 30-year yield is testing resistance levels at 4.77% (1-week high) and 4.792% (1-year high), with an RSI of 44.59 indicating no overbought condition. The breakout above the double-top neckline at 4.712% signals further upside potential. A critical test comes on Thursday when the U.S. Department of the Treasury auctions $22 billion in bonds, which will gauge market demand. Meanwhile, equity markets show mixed signals: the S&P 500 and Nasdaq rose 0.3% and 0.6%, respectively, while the Dow Jones fell 0.2%. The U.S. Dollar Index gained 0.4% to 98.13. Notably, both gold and oil rose—gold up 1.7% to a record high of approximately $3,980 and oil up 1.5% to $61.75—suggesting investors are simultaneously seeking safety and hedging against inflation. The latest Treasury Yield 30 Years Index analysis from October 6, 2025, urges immediate action, posing the question: should investors buy or sell?

title: 3年期美債殖利率微幅下滑、「2因素」撐盤 辣媽：政府關門消息影響會放大 | 聯合新聞網
content: U.S. Treasury bonds rose on Tuesday, October 7, 2025, continuing a recent mild upward trend. The auction of three-year U.S. notes, with a $58 billion issuance amount and a winning bid rate of 3.576%, outperformed market expectations, as the rate was nearly one basis point lower than the market quote just before bidding closed, indicating strong investor demand. Two key factors supported market demand: first, yields had risen significantly over the past month, attracting yield-seeking arbitrage traders; second, market consensus expects the Federal Reserve to cut interest rates in both October and December 2025. With many economic data releases delayed during this period, market expectations for growth and inflation lack timely data support, amplifying the impact of other international events. For example, prior to the auction, shifting political situations in Japan and France led to a surge in trading volume for 10-year Treasury futures. The three-year auction results were positive, and market attention will now shift to the upcoming 10-year and 30-year Treasury auctions on Wednesday and Thursday. The prevailing market expectation remains that the Fed will deliver two rate cuts by year-end, totaling 200 basis points.
